summary: Requests that RFC 1745, BGP4/IDRP for IP---OSPF Interaction, be moved to Historic status because the technology was never deployed in the public internet.

eli5.summary: It says a plan that never got used should be moved to the museum shelf.

questions: why was bgp4 idrp ospf never deployed
subtitle: Retiring a BGP4 and IDRP protocol specification that was never deployed.

tldr.problem: RFC 1745 describes BGP4/IDRP OSPF interaction, a complex routing protocol interaction that was never deployed in the public internet despite being a Proposed Standard for years.
tldr.mechanism: This document requests that RFC 1745 be moved to Historic status to reflect its actual non-deployment and lack of practical interest.
tldr.outcome: The specification is retired. Networks should not attempt to implement this mechanism for routing between BGP, IDRP and OSPF protocols.

today: RFC 1745 is now Historic. This RFC, 3167, documents that status change.

sections.title: An Abandoned Routing Design
sections.content:
RFC 1745 specified an interaction between BGP4 (Border Gateway Protocol version 4), IDRP (Interdomain Routing Protocol), and OSPF (Open Shortest Path First) routing protocols. This mechanism was designed to handle the routing coexistence challenges of the 1990s, when both BGP and IDRP were being considered as interdomain routing solutions.

However, RFC 1745 was never deployed in the public internet. Despite years as a Proposed Standard, no implementations emerged because the complexity was high and the practical need never materialized.
sections.eli5: Long ago, people designed a way for three different route-sharing systems to work together. But the Internet went a different way and nobody ever built it.

sections.title: Why This Design Was Never Used
sections.content:
The BGP4/IDRP OSPF interaction would require significant implementation complexity. In practice, BGP4 emerged as the clear choice for interdomain routing, and IDRP never gained real traction. The interaction mechanism became irrelevant as the routing landscape simplified.

Moving RFC 1745 to Historic status acknowledges this reality. A specification that was never deployed after years of opportunity should not remain as a recommended standard.
sections.eli5: The design was too complicated, and the problem it solved never really happened. The Internet picked a simpler solution instead.

sections.title: Impact
sections.content: Moving RFC 1745 to Historic status has no known effect on the security of the internet. Since this mechanism was never deployed, retiring it does not affect any existing networks or systems.
sections.eli5: This change has no effect on how the Internet works, because this mechanism was never part of it.

references.text: Varadhan, K., Hares, S. and Y. Rekhter, "BGP4/IDRP for IP---OSPF Interaction", RFC 1745, December 1994.
